transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

Well, I guess what brought me in is that... some nights after work, or maybe after a tense dinner, I'll start eating and it just feels like the decision-making part of me shuts off completely. It's like I can actually see myself reaching for more food, but I just can't make myself stop.
When that happens, do you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

Yeah, I do. On the bad nights, I can eat a full plate of dinner leftovers, and then... I'll just keep going. I'll go through a loaf of bread, whatever snacks are in the pantry, maybe a pint of ice cream. It all happens pretty fast, usually within an hour or two. It's definitely way more than I'd ever eat if someone else were sitting there with me.
After these eating episodes, do you ever make yourself vomit to try to undo them?

Yeah... I do. Usually it's late, after everyone goes to bed. I'll go into the bathroom and make myself throw up, or... sometimes I'll take laxatives. I just tell myself it’s a way to undo the damage from what I just ate. But honestly, right after I do it, I just feel really embarrassed. And physically kind of shaky.
How often do these binge-and-purge episodes happen?

For the last few months, it's been happening... I'd say most weeks. I'll have one of those nights where the eating just gets completely out of control. And then, you know, I try to make up for it. I'll throw up, or take those laxatives I mentioned. Sometimes I'll just skip meals the next day, or force myself to go on a really long walk to try and burn it off.

latest_inference.note: Recurrent objective binge episodes with compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting, laxatives, fasting, excessive exercise) occurring most weeks for months narrows the diagnosis to bulimia nervosa and rules out residual/unspecified eating disorder categories.
